narrative.overview:
A dark spine runs down the left of every screen and never changes. Everything to its right is bright, white, and dense with fact. The rail is the instrument; the workspace is the readout. An operator glances left to know where they are and looks right to read what is true, and the two never compete for attention.

The workspace is deliberately busy - this is a console for people who manage hundreds of endpoints. What keeps density from becoming noise is that colour is rationed. Most of a screen is near-black text on white with hairline rules. Colour appears only where it carries meaning: a severity, or the one accent.

v3 simplified the previous language rather than replacing its idea: one accent where there were two, five severities where there were nine hues, five type sizes where there were three ramps, three radii where there were six. Every page is composed from one kit, and a browser-side harmony gate measures every routed page against the token allowlist.
keyCharacteristics: A permanent dark rail (232px) against a cool-white workspace
One accent, the only colour on the page that is not a severity or a grey
Five severities, each with a wash and an icon, so colour is never the only carrier
Every ratio computed in CI, never asserted in prose; every page measured in a browser

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: There is one accent and it is the only colour on the page that does not mean a severity. A control that navigates, reveals or commits is the accent; nothing else is. The previous 'azure informs, magenta commits' rule is retired with the magenta.

rules.name: The Rationed Hue Rule
rules.body: A colour must be carrying information. If a hue could be swapped for grey without losing meaning, it should be grey.

rules.name: The Second Carrier Rule
rules.body: Colour is never the only carrier. Every severity pill carries its icon; a tile's kind is carried by its wash and its label; the active rail item is carried by white text and the lifted ground, not only by its accent edge.

rules.name: The Two Grounds Rule
rules.body: No accent is safe on both the rail and the page. The accent is 5.81:1 on white and 3.04:1 on the rail; the rail tones are the mirror image. On the rail the accent is an edge, never text.

rules.name: The Absent Zero Rule
rules.body: Unmeasured is drawn as absent: n/a, no arc, no bar, a hollow pip. Never as a measured 0, and never in the ok colour.

rules.name: The Floor Is The Ramp's Smallest Step
rules.body: Nothing renders below --t-cap, 10.5px - not in a stylesheet, not inline in JSX. CI enforces both halves. The caption is legible at that size only because every caption pair is graded at 4.5:1.

rules.name: The Label Leads Rule
rules.body: On a tile the caption sits above the figure. The number is bigger, but the word is what makes it mean anything.

rules.name: The Flat-Until-Touched Rule
rules.body: Surfaces rest almost flat. A hover changes the ground or the border, and a hover that changes only a border must step it at least 2:1 so the eye registers it.

dos: Do edit docs/design/itms-prototype-v3.html first. tokens.test.ts requires its :root to match the first :root of frontend/src/index.css exactly; the design file is the authority and the console is the transcription. Leave a comment beside a changed value naming the old value, the new value and the measured ratio.
Do compute every contrast ratio with the helper in frontend/src/test/contrast.test.ts and add the pair to the table matching its floor - 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for a control boundary or state.
Do name the v3 token (--sev-crit, --muted, --r-ctl) in new code. The legacy aliases exist so old code keeps resolving; a module is finished migrating when it reads none of them.
Do give every pill its icon and every unmeasured value its n/a.
Do give every tile, KPI and figure a destination. A number an operator cannot click is a number they cannot act on.
Do run node scripts/harmony.mjs on the routes you touched. It is the browser's opinion of whether the page is on the allowlist.
donts: Don't paint --line or --line-2 as a control boundary. They measure 1.23:1 and 1.49:1; the criterion asks 3:1 and the boundary scan in contrast.test.ts grades every rule that names a control.
Don't introduce a second accent, or reach for the retired magenta, violet, gold or teal by name. They alias to the one accent or to a severity.
Don't write a font size or a radius as a literal. 14, 16, 18 and 20px are not on the ramp; 8, 12, 14 and 16px are not on the ladder; the harmony gate reports each as a stray.
Don't type uppercase copy or an em dash into UI text. Captions are uppercased by CSS; sentence case everywhere else.
Don't ship a dead control in the chrome. No bell, no '+ New'.
Don't reference an undefined token with a fallback (var(--brand, #6d4aff)). Two of those shipped, both silently painting a retired colour for months.
Don't widen a guard to make a colour pass. Change the colour, in the design file, first.
